availableCommands.name: aws-cloudwatch-grafana-integration
availableCommands.description: Edits Terraform files in an AWS repository to enable Grafana access to CloudWatch metrics, following Swiss Post's internal standards. Use this skill whenever the user wants to connect Grafana to CloudWatch, add the Grafana Terraform provider, set up a CloudWatch data source in Grafana, integrate Grafana with an AWS account, configure the grafana-role module, or migrate from an old Grafana instance to the new one. Also trigger when the user mentions TFE workspace variables for Grafana, `FoundationRoleForGrafana`, or `grafana_auth`.

availableCommands.name: aws-route53-dns
availableCommands.description: Generates Terraform DNS records (CNAME and A) for AWS Route53 in the Swiss Post AWS Landing Zone (CF Palladium accounts). Use this skill whenever a user wants to create a DNS record in AWS, register a service endpoint in Route53, point a domain alias to a database/service endpoint in AWS, map an IP address to a hostname, or work with private hosted zones in Swiss Post's pnetcloud.ch domain — even if they just say "I need a DNS entry in AWS", "how do I add a hostname for my RDS", or "I need to point a name to an IP". This skill covers the Terraform code to create the record and where to place it in the repository. Invoke this skill any time the user mentions Route53, CNAME, A record, DNS records, private_hosted_zone, pnetcloud.ch, or creating a hostname/alias/IP mapping in an AWS CF Palladium account.

availableCommands.name: cf-jira-epic-writer
availableCommands.description: Creates JIRA Epics that conform to Swiss Post's company style for the CLOUD project in the Cloud Foundation cluster. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, draft, or write a JIRA Epic — even if they just say "create an epic", "write a new epic", "I need an epic for X", or "add a JIRA epic". This skill handles the full workflow: gathering Epic details, structuring the description according to Swiss Post conventions, setting the right components/labels/fix versions, and creating the Epic in JIRA via MCP.

availableCommands.name: cf-jira-story-writer
availableCommands.description: Creates JIRA Stories that conform to Swiss Post's company style for the CLOUD project in the Cloud Foundation cluster. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, draft, or write a JIRA Story — even if they just say "create a story", "write a new story", "I need a story for X", "add a story to epic Y", or "break down this epic into stories". This skill handles the full workflow: gathering Story details from the user (or deriving them from an existing Epic), structuring the description as a user story sentence, writing the Definition of Ready / Definition of Done / Acceptance Criteria in the correct ADF checklist format, setting story points, components, fix version, and parent Epic, and creating the Story in JIRA via MCP.

availableCommands.name: nvim-marginal-setup
availableCommands.description: Installs, configures and troubleshoots nvim-marginal, the AI writing copilot for Neovim, including its Confluence publishing via the Copilot CLI and the Atlassian MCP server. Use this skill whenever the user wants to install nvim-marginal, set up marginal in Neovim, link the plugin into their Neovim config, configure confluence.space_id or parent_id, fix ":MarginalConfluenceDraft" errors, find a Confluence space id or parent page id, set up the local ollama "fast" backend, install a Nerd Font for the heat overlay and pane icons, or diagnose missing glyphs, missing pandoc, or a missing Atlassian MCP server. Also trigger on "set up marginal", "install nvim-marginal", "publish my doc to Confluence from Neovim", or "marginal isn't working".

availableCommands.name: prompt-master
availableCommands.description: Generates optimized prompts for AI tools. Activates only when the user explicitly asks to write, fix, improve, or adapt a prompt for a specific AI tool (LLM, Cursor, Midjourney, image AI, video AI, coding agents, etc.). Does not activate for general conversation, coding tasks, document writing, or other non-prompt-engineering work.

availableCommands.name: rocky
availableCommands.description: Analyzes your Jira board and tells you exactly what to ship and what to unblock — broken down by today, next week, next month, and the current PI. Use rocky whenever you want to know what to focus on, what's overdue, what's blocked, or what's coming up in your sprint or PI. Also surfaces orphaned items — tickets assigned to you across all projects with no sprint, no due date, and no fix version. Trigger phrases include: "rocky", "what do I need to push today", "what should I work on this week", "show me my Jira priorities", "what's on my plate this PI", "what's overdue", "what's blocked in Jira", "what do I need to deliver this month", "give me my push list", "what orphaned items do I have in Jira", "show me my unscheduled work", "quick wins", "find quick wins for my stories", "what can I ship today", "what's closest to done", "show diff", "what moved", "orphaned cleanup", "search for orphaned epics".

availableCommands.name: skill-creator
availableCommands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

availableCommands.name: terraform-aws-acm
availableCommands.description: Use when obtaining SSL/TLS certificates on AWS in Swiss Post's Cloud Foundation (CF Palladium). Triggers on: request an SSL certificate on AWS, create an ACM certificate, use AWS Certificate Manager, add HTTPS to a load balancer, use the acm/aws Terraform module, obtain a wildcard certificate on AWS, obtain a host certificate on AWS, set up TLS on an ALB or NLB, use tfe.pnet.ch/postch/acm/aws. Covers host and wildcard certificate issuance via the Post private CA, and wiring the certificate to an aws_lb_listener.

availableCommands.name: terraform-aws-vm
availableCommands.description: Use when deploying Linux or Windows virtual machines on AWS in the Swiss Post Cloud Foundation (CF Palladium). Triggers on: deploy a VM on AWS, create an EC2 instance, provision a Linux server on AWS, provision a Windows server on AWS, use the linuxvm or windowsvm Terraform module, deploy RHEL on AWS, deploy Windows Server on AWS, set up a server in an AWS account, write Terraform for an EC2 server. Covers the linuxvm (tfe.pnet.ch/postch/linuxvm/aws) and windowsvm (tfe.pnet.ch/postch/windowsvm/aws) modules including required variables, Route53 DNS provider setup, hostname constraints, patch window selection, and operator tag validation.

availableCommands.name: terraform-azure-vm
availableCommands.description: Use when deploying Linux or Windows virtual machines on Azure in Swiss Post's Cloud Foundation (CF Palladium, Mainland). Triggers on: deploy a VM on Azure, provision a Linux server on Azure, provision a Windows server on Azure, use the linuxserver or windowsvm Terraform module for Azure, deploy RHEL on Azure, set up a Windows Server in an Azure subscription, write Terraform for an Azure virtual machine. Covers the linuxserver (tfe.pnet.ch/postch/linuxserver/azurerm) and windowsvm (tfe.pnet.ch/postch/windowswm/azurerm) modules including CMK disk encryption, private hosted zone DNS, patch windows, operator tags, availability zones, and staging configuration.

availableCommands.name: aws-cloudwatch-grafana-integration
availableCommands.description: Edits Terraform files in an AWS repository to enable Grafana access to CloudWatch metrics, following Swiss Post's internal standards. Use this skill whenever the user wants to connect Grafana to CloudWatch, add the Grafana Terraform provider, set up a CloudWatch data source in Grafana, integrate Grafana with an AWS account, configure the grafana-role module, or migrate from an old Grafana instance to the new one. availableCommands.name: aws-route53-dns
availableCommands.description: Generates Terraform DNS records (CNAME and A) for AWS Route53 in the Swiss Post AWS Landing Zone (CF Palladium accounts). Use this skill whenever a user wants to create a DNS record in AWS, register a service endpoint in Route53, point a domain alias to a database/service endpoint in AWS, map an IP address to a hostname, or work with private hosted zones in Swiss Post's pnetcloud.ch domain — even if they just say "I need a DNS entry in AWS", "how do I add a hostname for my RDS", or "I need to point a name to an IP". This skill covers the Terraform code to create the record and where to place it in the repository. Invoke this skill any time the user mentions Route53, CNAME, A record, DNS records, private_hosted_zone, pnetcloud.ch, or creating a hostname/alias/IP mapping in an AWS CF Palladium account.

availableCommands.name: cf-jira-epic-writer
availableCommands.description: Creates JIRA Epics that conform to Swiss Post's company style for the CLOUD project in the Cloud Foundation cluster. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, draft, or write a JIRA Epic — even if they just say "create an epic", "write a new epic", "I need an epic for X", or "add a JIRA epic". This skill handles the full workflow: gathering Epic details, structuring the description according to Swiss Post conventions, setting the right components/labels/fix versions, and creating the Epic in JIRA via MCP.

availableCommands.name: cf-jira-story-writer
availableCommands.description: Creates JIRA Stories that conform to Swiss Post's company style for the CLOUD project in the Cloud Foundation cluster. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, draft, or write a JIRA Story — even if they just say "create a story", "write a new story", "I need a story for X", "add a story to epic Y", or "break down this epic into stories". This skill handles the full workflow: gathering Story details from the user (or deriving them from an existing Epic), structuring the description as a user story sentence, writing the Definition of Ready / Definition of Done / Acceptance Criteria in the correct ADF checklist format, setting story points, components, fix version, and parent Epic, and creating the Story in JIRA via MCP.

availableCommands.name: nvim-marginal-setup
availableCommands.description: Installs, configures and troubleshoots nvim-marginal, the AI writing copilot for Neovim, including its Confluence publishing via the Copilot CLI and the Atlassian MCP server. Use this skill whenever the user wants to install nvim-marginal, set up marginal in Neovim, link the plugin into their Neovim config, configure confluence.space_id or parent_id, fix ":MarginalConfluenceDraft" errors, find a Confluence space id or parent page id, set up the local ollama "fast" backend, install a Nerd Font for the heat overlay and pane icons, or diagnose missing glyphs, missing pandoc, or a missing Atlassian MCP server. Also trigger on "set up marginal", "install nvim-marginal", "publish my doc to Confluence from Neovim", or "marginal isn't working".

availableCommands.name: rocky
availableCommands.description: Analyzes your Jira board and tells you exactly what to ship and what to unblock — broken down by today, next week, next month, and the current PI. Use rocky whenever you want to know what to focus on, what's overdue, what's blocked, or what's coming up in your sprint or PI. Also surfaces orphaned items — tickets assigned to you across all projects with no sprint, no due date, and no fix version. Trigger phrases include: "rocky", "what do I need to push today", "what should I work on this week", "show me my Jira priorities", "what's on my plate this PI", "what's overdue", "what's blocked in Jira", "what do I need to deliver this month", "give me my push list", "what orphaned items do I have in Jira", "show me my unscheduled work", "quick wins", "find quick wins for my stories", "what can I ship today", "what's closest to done", "show diff", "what moved", "orphaned cleanup", "search for orphaned epics".

availableCommands.name: terraform-aws-acm
availableCommands.description: Use when obtaining SSL/TLS certificates on AWS in Swiss Post's Cloud Foundation (CF Palladium). Triggers on: request an SSL certificate on AWS, create an ACM certificate, use AWS Certificate Manager, add HTTPS to a load balancer, use the acm/aws Terraform module, obtain a wildcard certificate on AWS, obtain a host certificate on AWS, set up TLS on an ALB or NLB, use tfe.pnet.ch/postch/acm/aws. Covers host and wildcard certificate issuance via the Post private CA, and wiring the certificate to an aws_lb_listener.

availableCommands.name: terraform-aws-vm
availableCommands.description: Use when deploying Linux or Windows virtual machines on AWS in the Swiss Post Cloud Foundation (CF Palladium). Triggers on: deploy a VM on AWS, create an EC2 instance, provision a Linux server on AWS, provision a Windows server on AWS, use the linuxvm or windowsvm Terraform module, deploy RHEL on AWS, deploy Windows Server on AWS, set up a server in an AWS account, write Terraform for an EC2 server. Covers the linuxvm (tfe.pnet.ch/postch/linuxvm/aws) and windowsvm (tfe.pnet.ch/postch/windowsvm/aws) modules including required variables, Route53 DNS provider setup, hostname constraints, patch window selection, and operator tag validation.

availableCommands.name: terraform-azure-vm
availableCommands.description: Use when deploying Linux or Windows virtual machines on Azure in Swiss Post's Cloud Foundation (CF Palladium, Mainland). Triggers on: deploy a VM on Azure, provision a Linux server on Azure, provision a Windows server on Azure, use the linuxserver or windowsvm Terraform module for Azure, deploy RHEL on Azure, set up a Windows Server in an Azure subscription, write Terraform for an Azure virtual machine. Covers the linuxserver (tfe.pnet.ch/postch/linuxserver/azurerm) and windowsvm (tfe.pnet.ch/postch/windowswm/azurerm) modules including CMK disk encryption, private hosted zone DNS, patch windows, operator tags, availability zones, and staging configuration.
